A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix E report original C++ runtime and clustering-cost experiments on binarized MNIST, IRIS and DIGITS, including cost variances.

after.justification: Section 4 retains original empirical results, and Appendix F adds measured preprocessing and sampling runtimes on KDD and SUSY, including comparisons with AFKMC2.

M1.justification: The quantum routines receive localized procedural revisions. V2 Appendix B.2 replaces cost-based sampling normalization with division by 2ζ, removing the preceding cost-estimation stage; Appendix D also revises sampling normalization and increases cost-estimation sampling requirements. The classical QI-k-means++ procedure and overall approximation-scheme architecture remain unchanged.

E1.justification: V2 adds evaluations on KDD, with 145,751 points and 74 features, and SUSY, with 5,000,000 points and 18 features (Appendix F.1). This substantially broadens the evaluated data beyond the original MNIST, IRIS and DIGITS coverage. DIGITS remains represented by its retained variance table.

E2.justification: V1 empirically compares QI-k-means++ only with ordinary k-means++. V2 additionally evaluates the fast seeding method AFKMC2 on KDD and SUSY in Table 5, substantially strengthening the empirical comparator set.

E3.justification: The added experiments measure preprocessing and sampling separately, test sampling at k = 5, 10, 50, 100 and 200, and use AFKMC2 with Markov-chain length 200. Cumulative timing for k = 2 through 10 is also reported. The original Section 4 experimental settings are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix F.1 extends the runtime sensitivity analysis through k = 200 and separately examines preprocessing versus sampling costs. Tables 4–5 support discussion of quadratic dependence on k and the setup/sampling tradeoff with AFKMC2. This is a focused extension of the existing computational analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over five runs, randomly selected seeds and identical clustering-cost variance tables for MNIST, IRIS and DIGITS. V2 introduces no new empirical uncertainty-reporting practice, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial timing evidence: Table 5 reports SUSY sampling times at k = 200 of 0.43 seconds for QI-k-means++, 1.2 for AFKMC2 and 195 for k-means++, excluding setup. Existing MNIST/IRIS costs, runtime plots and all three variance tables are unchanged. The DIGITS mean-cost table and runtime plot are removed.

T1.justification: The quantum derivations are materially revised, including normalized ancilla amplitudes, acceptance probabilities and an explicit known-aspect-ratio-bound assumption. Cost estimation changes from ζ² ln(10L)/ε² samples in v1 Appendix C.5 to O(ζ⁴ ln(10L)/ε²) in v2 Appendix D.5. Theorem 4 consequently replaces quadratic aspect-ratio dependence with ζ^O(1).

C1.justification: The main contributions—quantum D²-sampling, its classical dequantization and a quantum approximation scheme with polylogarithmic dependence on N—are retained. However, Theorem 4's advertised runtime guarantee is weakened from ζ² dependence to an unspecified polynomial dependence on ζ.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretation of QI-k-means++ versus AFKMC2: faster sampling accompanies more expensive preprocessing, with different implications for updating data. The new conclusion identifies widely separated clusters as a setting where the relevant aspect-ratio-like parameters can become large and discusses improving these dependencies.

D1.justification: Appendix F.1 documents AFKMC2's chain length of 200, the added datasets' sizes and dimensions, and separate setup times. Conversely, v1's DIGITS dataset description and source attribution disappear even though its variance table remains. The original C++ and hardware disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: Section 1.1 and Table 1 expand the existing positioning against K-MC2, AFK-MC2 and rejection sampling through explicit parameter and approximation tradeoffs. Six references are added, including closest-pair methods, quantum background, the new datasets and Jaiswal et al. (2014), which resolves a missing attribution. The scikit-learn reference is removed.

P1.justification: V2 reorganizes the existing comparison into its own subsection, adds a conclusion, acknowledgements and quantum preliminaries, and revises author presentation and citation style. These are localized structural and explanatory changes; most existing method and proof prose remains closely matched.

P2.justification: V2 changes typography, margins and spacing throughout, adds a theoretical comparison table, two timing tables and two runtime plots, and removes the DIGITS mean-cost table and plot. Retained MNIST/IRIS plots receive numbered captions and are relocated. Together these substantially revise the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 improves claim–proof consistency through revised sampling normalization and more conservative cost-estimation bounds, while adding useful large-dataset timing comparisons with AFKMC2. The benefit is limited by missing clustering-cost comparisons for the added baseline and the removal of DIGITS means/runtime reporting despite retaining its variances. The evidence supports a positive but limited overall quality gain.
